tip: Dropping 'denn' into a question makes it sound curious and friendly rather than blunt: 'warum fragst du denn' softens the tone without changing the literal meaning.
'Ja wohl' adds an indignant 'surely, obviously': 'das ist ja wohl das Mindeste' = that is surely the very least you can expect.
Reported speech often uses a special verb form: 'beweise' instead of 'beweist' marks the statement as the professor's claim, not the narrator's own fact.
Here 'eben' means just or simply and marks resigned acceptance: 'dann machen wir es eben auf deine Art' signals giving in to how things are.
The verb 'bedürfen' takes a genitive object: 'es bedarf einer gründlichen Analyse'. It is a formal way of saying something is needed.
In a yes/no question, 'etwa' adds disbelief and usually expects the answer no: 'hast du etwa die ganze Torte allein aufgegessen' carries a note of accusation.
Here 'ruhig' means go ahead or it would have been fine to: 'du hättest ruhig etwas sagen können'. It has nothing to do with quiet.
'Lassen' plus an infinitive here means having something done for you, not doing it yourself: 'restaurieren lassen' = had it restored.
'Ja' in 'das ist ja unglaublich' stresses the fact as plain to see, a reaction, with no separate word in English.
'Doch mal' warms a bare command into a friendly invite: 'komm doch mal vorbei' softens 'komm vorbei' to why don't you drop by.
'Guck mal' is a casual 'look!' used to draw someone's attention.
'Denn nur' in a question adds impatience or worry: 'wo bleibt er denn nur' = where on earth is he.
